name: pdf-inspector
description: Fast Rust library for PDF inspection, classification, and text extraction. Intelligently detects scanned vs text-based PDFs to enable smart routing decisions.
one_liner: A fast tool that looks at a PDF and instantly tells you whether it's real text or a scanned image, then pulls out clean text without expensive OCR when it can.
buyer: A document-heavy SaaS — invoicing, legal, or insurance — that's paying to run every PDF through OCR even when most of them don't need it.
business_use_cases: An invoice-processing startup routes incoming PDFs through it first, skipping OCR costs on the roughly half that are already text-based.
A legal-tech company speeds up contract ingestion by extracting clean, position-aware text before running its AI review.
A document-management SaaS uses it to auto-tag uploads as 'searchable' versus 'needs OCR' to improve search quality.

money_ideas.idea: Run a hosted 'upload a PDF, get clean Markdown plus a scanned/text verdict' API and charge per page.
License it as a paid tier feature inside an existing document-management SaaS.

steal_this: Build a tiny hosted API this weekend that returns clean Markdown plus a scanned/text verdict for any uploaded PDF, and charge per page — undercut OCR-only competitors on cost.
